## Why this analysis

The drug-target layer of the fasting vs 2 h glucose analysis found that T2D liability acting
through the KATP channel (KCNJ11/ABCC8, the sulfonylurea target) was associated with higher AD risk
(OR 1.27 per log-odds of T2D, SlopeHunter-corrected Bellenguez). At the variant level the estimate
rests on two of seven instruments: **rs5215** in KCNJ11 (a proxy for the E23K coding variant,
rs5219) and the low-frequency **rs113264182** (nearest gene NCR3LG1). The amylin result fell apart
in the same view, being driven by one variant with its own AD association.

A drug-target effect predicts that the variant raising T2D risk through the channel is the **same**
variant that raises AD risk. A nearby but distinct AD signal predicts two different causal
variants. This notebook tests that at the locus:

1. **The instruments variant by variant** for the KATP channel and, for comparison, the amylin
   receptor.
2. **Regional association** for T2D and AD, coloured by LD with rs5215.
3. **LD among the lead variants**, including rs5219 (E23K).
4. **Colocalisation** (`coloc.abf`, one causal variant per trait) between T2D and each AD dataset,
   with a prior sensitivity analysis, and **SuSiE-based colocalisation** allowing more than one
   causal variant.
5. **Heterogeneity** among the seven KATP instruments.
6. **Kunkle at the variant level** for the leads.
7. The chr17q21 (MLX) signal behind the amylin estimate.
8. **KATP specificity:** AD per mmol/L of 2 h glucose for KATP against GCK and genome-wide beta-cell variants, with Uffelmann 2026 as replication.
9. **The vascular KATP channel** (ABCC9/KCNJ8): a regional lookup.

Data come from the targets pipeline store (`_targets/`): Suzuki 2024 T2D (European), Bellenguez
2022 AD raw and SlopeHunter-corrected, Kunkle 2019 AD. All positions are GRCh37. LD is from the
1000 Genomes European panel (503 people) the pipeline uses everywhere.

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(data.table)
library(knitr)
library(targets)

# Pipeline helpers: ld_matrix(), resolve_plink2(), harmonise conventions.
for (f in list.files("pipeline/R", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
cfg    <- yaml::read_yaml("pipeline/config.yml")
plink2 <- resolve_plink2(cfg$paths$plink2)
bfile  <- cfg$paths$ld_bfile
bim    <- tar_read(ld_bim)

# ---- settings: edit here -------------------------------------------------------------------
region   <- list(chr = "11", start = 17.0e6, end = 17.8e6)   # KCNJ11 17.41 Mb, ABCC8 17.41-17.50 Mb
leads    <- c("rs5215", "rs5219", "rs113264182")
datasets <- c(t2d    = "gwas_t2d_suzuki_eur",
              ad_sh  = "gwas_sh_ad_bellenguez",
              ad_raw = "gwas_ad_bellenguez",
              ad_kun = "gwas_ad_kunkle")
labels   <- c(t2d = "T2D (Suzuki 2024)", ad_sh = "AD, Bellenguez (SlopeHunter)",
              ad_raw = "AD, Bellenguez (raw)", ad_kun = "AD, Kunkle (clinical)")
# Case/control counts (for coloc's case fraction); T2D uses the per-variant effective N with s = 0.5.
cc <- list(ad_sh = c(n = 487511, s = 85934 / 487511), ad_raw = c(n = 487511, s = 85934 / 487511),
           ad_kun = c(n = 63926, s = 21982 / 63926))
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

theme_fm <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

## 1. The instruments, variant by variant

Each point is one drug-target instrument: its effect on T2D (x) against its effect on AD (y), both on
the T2D risk allele, with 95% intervals (SlopeHunter-corrected Bellenguez). Labels give the nearest
protein-coding gene and the rsID; where the nearest gene is not the drug-target gene the variant was
assigned to (within 100 kb), the target is shown in brackets. The solid red line through the origin is the
class estimate from the drug-target layer (`drug_target_results.csv`), which allows for the residual
LD between variants, so it is not simply a fit to the points as drawn.

The amylin receptor panel is the comparison case: its estimate rests on one variant (rs34779241,
nearest gene PLEKHH3) with an AD association of its own, while the CALCR variant is flat. That is
the pattern of a nearby variant acting on AD independently of the target, which is why the KATP
locus gets the closer look below.

```{r scatter-data}
class_labels <- c(katp_secretagogue = "KATP channel (sulfonylureas)", amylin = "Amylin receptor")
dt_snps <- read_csv("results/pipeline/contrast/drug_target_snps.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(set == "primary", outcome == "ad_bellenguez", arm == "slopehunter", drug_class %in% names(class_labels)) |>
  mutate(class = class_labels[drug_class],
         label = if_else(nearest_gene == drug_target_gene, sprintf("%s\n%s", nearest_gene, SNP),
                         sprintf("%s [%s]\n%s", nearest_gene, drug_target_gene, SNP)))
dt_lines <- read_csv("results/pipeline/contrast/drug_target_results.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(set == "primary", outcome == "ad_bellenguez", arm == "slopehunter", level == "class",
         trait == "AD (log-OR)", target %in% names(class_labels)) |>
  transmute(class = class_labels[target], slope = b,
            txt = sprintf("OR %.2f (%.2f, %.2f)\nper log-odds T2D", exp(b), exp(b - 1.96 * se), exp(b + 1.96 * se)))
```

```{r scatter, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
ggplot(dt_snps, aes(beta_t2d, beta_y)) +
  # zero axes, drawn first and heavier than the grid
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey15", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey15", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = beta_y - 1.96 * se_y, ymax = beta_y + 1.96 * se_y), colour = "grey70", width = 0) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = beta_t2d - 1.96 * se_t2d, xmax = beta_t2d + 1.96 * se_t2d), colour = "grey70",
```


## 2. Regional association

All four datasets are aligned to the LD panel's counted allele (so the signed LD below applies to
them directly). Palindromic variants (A/T, C/G) are dropped, since the Kunkle file has no allele
frequencies to resolve their strand.

```{r region-data}
in_region <- function(g) g[as.character(chr) == region$chr & pos >= region$start & pos <= region$end]
align_to_bim <- function(g) {
  m <- merge(g, bim[, .(SNP, a1, a2)], by = "SNP")
  m <- m[(ea == a1 & oa == a2) | (ea == a2 & oa == a1)]
  m[ea != a1, `:=`(beta = -beta, eaf = 1 - eaf)]
  m[!paste0(a1, a2) %chin% c("AT", "TA", "CG", "GC")][, .(SNP, pos, beta, se, p, eaf, n)]
}
reg <- purrr::imap(datasets, \(tgt, k) align_to_bim(in_region(tar_read_raw(tgt))))
common <- Reduce(intersect, purrr::map(reg, "SNP"))
reg <- purrr::map(reg, \(d) d[SNP %chin% common][order(pos)])

R <- ld_matrix(common, bim, bfile, plink2)          # signed r on the counted allele (a1)
common <- rownames(R)
reg <- purrr::map(reg, \(d) d[match(common, SNP)])
r2_lead <- R[, "rs5215"]^2

long <- purrr::imap_dfr(reg, \(d, k) tibble(dataset = labels[[k]], SNP = d$SNP, pos = d$pos, p = d$p)) |>
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = labels), r2 = r2_lead[SNP],
         r2_bin = cut(r2, c(-Inf, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, Inf), labels = c("<0.2", "0.2-0.4", "0.4-0.6", "0.6-0.8", ">0.8")))
genes <- tibble(gene = c("NCR3LG1", "KCNJ11", "ABCC8"), start = c(17373e3, 17406.8e3, 17414.4e3),
                end = c(17398e3, 17410.9e3, 17498.4e3))   # GRCh37, approximate
```

`r length(common)` variants are present in all four datasets.

```{r region-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=10}
ggplot(long, aes(pos / 1e6, -log10(p))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = genes$start / 1e6, xmax = genes$end / 1e6, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           alpha = 0.08, fill = "#00274c") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = r2_bin), size = 1.3) +
  geom_point(data = filter(long, SNP %in% leads), shape = 21, size = 3.5, colour = "black", stroke = 1) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = filter(long, SNP %in% leads), aes(label = SNP), size = 3.3, seed = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("<0.2" = "grey70", "0.2-0.4" = "#9fb4cc", "0.4-0.6" = "#4f7ba6",
                                 "0.6-0.8" = "#ffcb05", ">0.8" = "#9a3324")) +
  labs(x = "Chromosome 11 position (Mb, GRCh37); shaded: NCR3LG1, KCNJ11, ABCC8",
       y = expression(-log[10](p)), colour = "r² with rs5215") +
  theme_fm
```

```{r region-leads}
top <- purrr::imap_dfr(reg, \(d, k) d[which.min(p)] |> as_tibble() |> mutate(dataset = labels[[k]])) |>
  transmute(Dataset = dataset, `Top variant` = SNP, `Position` = pos, p = signif(p, 2),
            `r² with rs5215` = round(r2_lead[`Top variant`], 2))
kable(top, caption = "Strongest variant in the region, per dataset")
```

## 3. LD among the lead variants

```{r lead-ld}
ld_set <- intersect(unique(c(leads, top$`Top variant`)), common)
round(R[ld_set, ld_set]^2, 3) |> kable(caption = "r² (1000 Genomes European)")
```

## 4. Colocalisation

**Single causal variant (`coloc.abf`).** Five hypotheses: H0 no association, H1 T2D only, H2 AD
only, H3 both but different causal variants, H4 both with a shared causal variant. A drug-target
effect predicts H4; a nearby independent AD signal predicts H3. Default priors
(p1 = p2 = 1×10⁻⁴, p12 = 1×10⁻⁵).

```{r coloc-abf}
as_coloc <- function(d, k) {
  maf <- pmin(reg$t2d$eaf, 1 - reg$t2d$eaf)           # Kunkle has no frequencies; use T2D's
  if (k == "t2d") list(snp = d$SNP, beta = d$beta, varbeta = d$se^2, type = "cc", N = d$n, s = 0.5, MAF = maf)
  else list(snp = d$SNP, beta = d$beta, varbeta = d$se^2, type = "cc", N = cc[[k]][["n"]], s = cc[[k]][["s"]], MAF = maf)
}
abf <- purrr::map(c("ad_sh", "ad_raw", "ad_kun"), \(k)
  suppressMessages(coloc::coloc.abf(as_coloc(reg$t2d, "t2d"), as_coloc(reg[[k]], k)))) |>
  setNames(c("ad_sh", "ad_raw", "ad_kun"))

purrr::imap_dfr(abf, \(r, k) as_tibble(as.list(r$summary)) |> mutate(Comparison = paste("T2D vs", labels[[k]]))) |>
  transmute(Comparison, SNPs = nsnps, across(PP.H0.abf:PP.H4.abf, \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  rename_with(\(x) sub("PP\\.(H[0-4])\\.abf", "\\1", x)) |>
  kable(caption = "Posterior probabilities")
```

```{r coloc-abf-snps}
# If a shared variant is supported, which one? Posterior for each SNP being the shared causal variant (H4).
purrr::imap_dfr(abf, \(r, k) r$results |> as_tibble() |> slice_max(SNP.PP.H4, n = 3) |>
                  transmute(Comparison = labels[[k]], SNP = snp, `PP (shared causal | H4)` = round(SNP.PP.H4, 3))) |>
  kable()
```

**Prior sensitivity.** How the conclusion depends on p12, the prior probability that a variant is
causal for both traits. The usual guidance treats H4 as robust only if it stays high for p12 down to
about 5×10⁻⁶.

```{r coloc-sensitivity, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
# Only H4's prior involves p12, so changing p12 rescales PP(H4) by new/old p12 and renormalises.
p12_grid <- 10^seq(-8, -4, by = 0.25)
sens <- purrr::imap_dfr(abf, \(r, k) {
  pp <- r$summary[paste0("PP.H", 0:4, ".abf")]
  purrr::map_dfr(p12_grid, \(p12) {
    w <- pp * c(1, 1, 1, 1, p12 / 1e-5); w <- w / sum(w)
    tibble(p12 = p12, H3 = w[[4]], H4 = w[[5]])
  }) |> mutate(dataset = labels[[k]])
}) |> pivot_longer(c(H3, H4), names_to = "hypothesis", values_to = "pp")

ggplot(sens, aes(p12, pp, colour = hypothesis)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1e-5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(H3 = "grey55", H4 = "#9a3324"),
                      labels = c(H3 = "H3: distinct causal variants", H4 = "H4: shared causal variant")) +
  labs(x = "p12 (prior that a variant is causal for both); dashed = default", y = "Posterior probability",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_fm
```

**More than one causal variant (SuSiE).** `coloc.abf` assumes one causal variant per trait. SuSiE
fine-maps each trait into 95% credible sets using the LD matrix, and colocalisation is then tested
between credible sets, so it needs at least one credible set **in each trait**. It is run on the two
AD datasets with ordinary GWAS statistics (raw Bellenguez and Kunkle). The SlopeHunter-corrected
statistics are a weighted difference of two GWAS and do not satisfy SuSiE's summary-statistic model,
so they are left out. The LD comes from 503 reference genomes, not the GWAS samples.

```{r susie}
ss_input <- function(d, k) { x <- c(as_coloc(d, k), list(LD = R)); x$N <- median(x$N); x }
ss_ad <- purrr::map(c(ad_raw = "ad_raw", ad_kun = "ad_kun"), \(k)
  tryCatch(coloc::runsusie(ss_input(reg[[k]], k), maxit = 1000), error = function(e) e))
purrr::imap_dfr(ss_ad, \(f, k) {
  if (inherits(f, "error")) return(tibble(Trait = labels[[k]], `Credible sets` = NA_integer_, note = conditionMessage(f)))
  tibble(Trait = labels[[k]], `Credible sets` = length(f$sets$cs),
         `Max PIP` = round(max(f$pip), 2), `Variant with max PIP` = names(f$pip)[which.max(f$pip)])
}) |> kable(caption = "SuSiE fine-mapping of AD in the region")
```

With no AD credible set, there is no AD signal for SuSiE to colocalise with T2D, so the
multi-variant analysis cannot add to `coloc.abf` here.

## 5. Heterogeneity among the seven KATP instruments

If the KATP channel drives AD through T2D liability, every instrument's AD effect should be
proportional to its T2D effect. Cochran's Q, generalised for the residual LD between instruments
(they were clumped at r² < 0.1):
$Q = (\hat\beta_Y - \hat\theta\hat\beta_X)^\top \Omega^{-1} (\hat\beta_Y - \hat\theta\hat\beta_X)$ with
$\Omega_{jk} = \sigma_{Yj}\sigma_{Yk} r_{jk}$.

```{r heterogeneity}
katp <- read_csv("results/pipeline/contrast/drug_target_snps.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(set == "primary", drug_class == "katp_secretagogue")
het <- katp |> group_by(outcome, arm) |> group_modify(\(x, ...) {
  Rk <- ld_matrix(x$SNP, bim, bfile, plink2); x <- x[match(rownames(Rk), x$SNP), ]
  s <- if_else(x$ea == bim$a1[match(x$SNP, bim$SNP)], 1, -1); Rk <- Rk * outer(s, s)
  Oi <- solve(outer(x$se_y, x$se_y) * Rk)
  th <- drop(t(x$beta_t2d) %*% Oi %*% x$beta_y) / drop(t(x$beta_t2d) %*% Oi %*% x$beta_t2d)
  e <- x$beta_y - th * x$beta_t2d; Q <- drop(t(e) %*% Oi %*% e)
  tibble(SNPs = nrow(x), theta = th, Q = Q, df = nrow(x) - 1, p_het = pchisq(Q, nrow(x) - 1, lower.tail = FALSE))
}) |> ungroup()
het |> transmute(Outcome = paste(outcome, arm), SNPs, `θ (log-OR AD per log-odds T2D)` = round(theta, 3),
                 Q = round(Q, 2), df, `p (heterogeneity)` = signif(p_het, 2)) |> kable()
```

## 6. Kunkle at the variant level

```{r kunkle-leads}
lead_tab <- katp |>
  filter(SNP %in% c("rs5215", "rs113264182")) |>
  transmute(SNP, nearest_gene, Outcome = paste(outcome, arm), b = beta_y, se = se_y,
            p = 2 * pnorm(-abs(beta_y / se_y)), beta_t2d)
lead_tab |>
  transmute(SNP, `Nearest gene` = nearest_gene, Outcome,
            `AD log-OR (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f, %.3f)", b, b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se),
            p = signif(p, 2), `Wald ratio (per log-odds T2D)` = round(b / beta_t2d, 2)) |>
  arrange(SNP, Outcome) |>
  kable()
```

## Reading the results: KCNJ11

**There is no detectable AD signal at the locus to colocalise.** `coloc.abf` puts about 90% on H1
(a T2D signal, no AD signal) in all three comparisons; H4 (shared causal variant) is 1–3% and H3
(distinct variants) 4–7%. The strongest AD variants in the region (p ≈ 10⁻³) lie about 300 kb away
at 17.7 Mb and are unlinked to rs5215 (r² ≤ 0.01). SuSiE finds no AD credible set. This is what a
real but small effect looks like as much as a null: an AD association of p = 0.04 at rs5215 is far
too weak for colocalisation, which needs a clear signal in both traits. So colocalisation neither
confirms nor refutes a shared variant here; it is underpowered by design for an effect this size.

**rs5215 behaves the same in every AD dataset.** Its AD log-OR is 0.017–0.018 in raw and
SlopeHunter-corrected Bellenguez and 0.017 in Kunkle, giving the same Wald ratio (0.25–0.27 per
log-odds of T2D) in all three. Kunkle's interval includes zero only because it is smaller. If the
variant were colocalising, this conditional posterior is where it would show: given a shared variant
(H4), rs5215 and its perfect proxy rs5219 (E23K, r² = 1.00) carry essentially all of the probability.

**rs113264182 does not replicate.** It is independent of rs5215 (r² = 0.02), positive in
Bellenguez (0.094, p = 0.007) but negative in Kunkle (−0.047). It drove the KATP class estimate up
in Bellenguez and, missing or reversed, pulled it to zero in Kunkle. The null Kunkle class estimate
is therefore about this variant, not about rs5215.

**The seven instruments are consistent with one effect** (heterogeneity p = 0.39 in SlopeHunter
Bellenguez, 0.50 raw, 0.28 Kunkle), so the five flat variants do not contradict the two positive
ones at this precision.

**Overall.** The best-supported reading is a small effect carried by the E23K haplotype
(rs5215/rs5219), consistent in direction and size across all three AD datasets but individually
only nominal. The KATP class estimate of OR 1.27 overstates it because of rs113264182, which looks
like noise. Colocalisation cannot settle whether rs5215 is causal for AD at this effect size; a
larger clinical AD dataset, or E23K carriers in a cohort with cognitive follow-up, would.

## 7. A second post-load locus? The chr17q21 (MLX) signal

The amylin-receptor estimate rested on one variant, rs34779241, labelled RAMP2 because RAMP2 was the
only drug-target gene within 100 kb. It is in fact a proxy (r² = 0.89) for **rs676387**, Suzuki
2024's index variant for the T2D locus named *MLX* (obesity cluster). In GTEx v8 it is an eQTL for
TUBG2 (22 tissues), CNTNAP1 (strongest in pancreas) and several other genes, but not for RAMP2. Like
the KCNJ11 variant, the T2D signal raises 2 h glucose with no fasting effect. The strongest AD
association nearby, however, sits on a partly correlated haplotype (lead rs12450136, r² ≈ 0.3)
with no 2 h glucose effect.

So the question is whether one causal variant raises T2D risk, 2 h glucose and AD together (a
second post-load locus), or whether AD is driven by a separate nearby variant that the T2D
instrument picks up through LD (pleiotropy). Here the AD signal is strong enough (p ≈ 10⁻⁵) for
colocalisation to have power. T2D vs 2 h glucose is included as a positive control: both should
share the index variant.

```{r mlx-data}
region17 <- list(chr = "17", start = 40.4e6, end = 41.2e6)
leads17  <- c("rs676387", "rs34779241", "rs12450136")
datasets17 <- c(t2d = "gwas_t2d_suzuki_eur", glu2h = "gwas_glu2h_chen", fg = "gwas_fg_chen",
                ad_sh = "gwas_sh_ad_bellenguez", ad_raw = "gwas_ad_bellenguez", ad_kun = "gwas_ad_kunkle")
labels17 <- c(t2d = "T2D (Suzuki 2024)", glu2h = "2 h glucose (Chen 2021)", fg = "Fasting glucose (Chen 2021)",
              ad_sh = labels[["ad_sh"]], ad_raw = labels[["ad_raw"]], ad_kun = labels[["ad_kun"]])
quant_n <- c(glu2h = 63396, fg = 200622)

in17 <- function(g) g[as.character(chr) == region17$chr & pos >= region17$start & pos <= region17$end]
reg17 <- purrr::map(datasets17, \(tgt) align_to_bim(in17(tar_read_raw(tgt))))
common17 <- Reduce(intersect, purrr::map(reg17, "SNP"))
R17 <- ld_matrix(common17, bim, bfile, plink2)
common17 <- rownames(R17)
reg17 <- purrr::map(reg17, \(d) d[match(common17, SNP)])

long17 <- purrr::imap_dfr(reg17, \(d, k) tibble(dataset = labels17[[k]], SNP = d$SNP, pos = d$pos, p = d$p)) |>
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = labels17), r2 = R17[SNP, "rs676387"]^2,
         r2_bin = cut(r2, c(-Inf, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, Inf), labels = c("<0.2", "0.2-0.4", "0.4-0.6", "0.6-0.8", ">0.8")))
genes17 <- tibble(gene = c("MLX", "TUBG2/PLEKHH3", "RAMP2"), start = c(40719086, 40811323, 40910465),
                  end = c(40725257, 40829048, 40915059))
```

`r length(common17)` variants are present in all six datasets.

```{r mlx-coloc}
maf17 <- pmin(reg17$t2d$eaf, 1 - reg17$t2d$eaf)
as_coloc17 <- function(k) {
  d <- reg17[[k]]
  base <- list(snp = d$SNP, beta = d$beta, varbeta = d$se^2, MAF = maf17)
  if (k == "t2d") c(base, list(type = "cc", N = d$n, s = 0.5))
  else if (k %in% names(quant_n)) c(base, list(type = "quant", N = quant_n[[k]]))
  else c(base, list(type = "cc", N = cc[[k]][["n"]], s = cc[[k]][["s"]]))
}
pairs17 <- tribble(~a, ~b,
  "t2d", "glu2h",            # positive control: should share the index variant
  "t2d", "ad_sh", "t2d", "ad_raw", "t2d", "ad_kun",
  "glu2h", "ad_sh", "glu2h", "ad_raw", "glu2h", "ad_kun")
abf17 <- purrr::pmap(pairs17, \(a, b) suppressMessages(coloc::coloc.abf(as_coloc17(a), as_coloc17(b))))
coloc17 <- purrr::map2_dfr(abf17, seq_len(nrow(pairs17)), \(r, i) {
  top <- r$results |> slice_max(SNP.PP.H4, n = 1)
  as_tibble(as.list(r$summary)) |>
    mutate(Comparison = paste(labels17[[pairs17$a[i]]], "vs", labels17[[pairs17$b[i]]]),
           `Top shared variant (if H4)` = sprintf("%s (%.2f)", top$snp, top$SNP.PP.H4))
})
coloc17 |>
  transmute(Comparison, across(PP.H0.abf:PP.H4.abf, \(x) round(x, 3)), `Top shared variant (if H4)`) |>
  rename_with(\(x) sub("PP\\.(H[0-4])\\.abf", "\\1", x)) |>
  kable(caption = "coloc.abf posterior probabilities (default priors)")
```

```{r mlx-sensitivity, fig.width=11, fig.height=4.5}
sens17 <- purrr::map2_dfr(abf17, seq_len(nrow(pairs17)), \(r, i) {
  pp <- r$summary[paste0("PP.H", 0:4, ".abf")]
  purrr::map_dfr(p12_grid, \(p12) { w <- pp * c(1, 1, 1, 1, p12 / 1e-5); w <- w / sum(w)
    tibble(p12 = p12, H3 = w[[4]], H4 = w[[5]]) }) |>
    mutate(comparison = paste(sub(" \\(.*", "", labels17[[pairs17$a[i]]]), "vs", labels17[[pairs17$b[i]]]))
}) |>
  filter(grepl("AD", comparison)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(H3, H4), names_to = "hypothesis", values_to = "pp")
ggplot(sens17, aes(p12, pp, colour = hypothesis)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1e-5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison, nrow = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(H3 = "grey55", H4 = "#9a3324"),
                      labels = c(H3 = "H3: distinct causal variants", H4 = "H4: shared causal variant")) +
  labs(x = "p12 (dashed = default)", y = "Posterior probability", colour = NULL) +
  theme_fm + theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 9))
```

**One AD signal or two?** `coloc.abf` assumes a single causal variant per trait, and SuSiE (which
relaxes that) did not converge with the reference LD here. A simpler, more robust check is an
approximate conditional analysis on the two candidate leads: the T2D index rs676387 and the top AD
variant rs72826906 (r² ≈ 0.27). For z-scores $z_1, z_2$ with signed LD $r$, the association of
variant 1 conditional on variant 2 is $z_{1\mid 2} = (z_1 - r z_2)/\sqrt{1 - r^2}$. If AD has one
signal on the T2D haplotype, rs676387 should keep its AD association after conditioning on
rs72826906; if AD's signal is on the other haplotype, it should not.

```{r mlx-conditional}
cond_pair <- function(k, s1, s2) {
  d <- reg17[[k]]; z <- setNames(d$beta / d$se, d$SNP); r <- R17[s1, s2]
  tibble(Trait = labels17[[k]], Variant = c(s1, s2),
         `z (marginal)` = c(z[[s1]], z[[s2]]),
         `z (conditional on the other)` = c((z[[s1]] - r * z[[s2]]) / sqrt(1 - r^2),
                                            (z[[s2]] - r * z[[s1]]) / sqrt(1 - r^2)))
}
purrr::map_dfr(c("t2d", "glu2h", "ad_sh", "ad_raw", "ad_kun"), cond_pair, s1 = "rs676387", s2 = "rs72826906") |>
  mutate(`p (marginal)` = signif(2 * pnorm(-abs(`z (marginal)`)), 2),
         `p (conditional)` = signif(2 * pnorm(-abs(`z (conditional on the other)`)), 2),
         across(starts_with("z ("), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  kable(caption = sprintf("Approximate conditional analysis (signed r = %.2f between the two variants, 1000 Genomes European)",
                          R17["rs676387", "rs72826906"]))
```


### Reading the results: chr17q21

**T2D and 2 h glucose share one signal.** The positive control works: T2D and 2 h glucose colocalise
(H4 = 0.90), and conditional on rs676387 the other haplotype's T2D association disappears (p = 0.58).
This is a post-load-specific T2D locus, as at KCNJ11.

**AD's signal sits mostly on the other haplotype.** The strongest AD variant (rs72826906, p = 6×10⁻⁶
SlopeHunter-corrected) keeps its association after conditioning on the T2D index (p = 0.004), while
the T2D index's AD association drops from p = 8×10⁻⁵ to 0.06. rs72826906 has no T2D or 2 h glucose
effect of its own once rs676387 is accounted for. So most of the AD association at this locus comes
from a variant that does not act through T2D or post-load glucose; the T2D variant picks it up through
LD (r² ≈ 0.27). A small residual AD effect on the T2D haplotype cannot be excluded.

**Why `coloc.abf` nonetheless leans to H4** (0.78 SlopeHunter-corrected, 0.50 raw): with a single
causal variant assumed per trait, the AD evidence at the T2D haplotype (p ≈ 10⁻⁴) is enough for the
default prior to favour sharing. The call is not robust: on the same posteriors, lowering p12 to
5×10⁻⁶ gives H4 ≈ 0.63 (SlopeHunter) and 0.33 (raw), and at 1×10⁻⁶ about 0.26 and 0.09. The
conditional analysis, which allows two variants, is the more reliable guide here.

**Kunkle shows nothing at either variant** (p > 0.2), as with the amylin class estimate.

**Overall.** This locus is not the amylin receptor: the variant is a proxy for the *MLX*-region T2D
index, is not an eQTL for RAMP2, and its AD association is largely explained by a neighbouring
variant without glycaemic effects. It does not add a second post-load locus to KCNJ11.

## 8. Is the KATP effect on AD larger than its glucose effect predicts?

If the KATP channel affects AD through something other than glucose, KATP variants should
give more AD per mmol/L of 2 h glucose than variants that raise glucose by other routes. The
cleanest comparison is glucokinase (GCK), which acts in the same cell through a different step of
the glucose-sensing pathway. The broader comparisons are the genome-wide beta-cell variants (Suzuki
clusters) and all primary T2D instruments. The KCNJ11/ABCC8 (chr11 16.9–17.9 Mb) and GCK (chr7
43.7–44.7 Mb) regions are left out of the genome-wide sets.

All estimates use the same T2D selection (Suzuki 2024). For each group, AD and 2 h glucose are each
regressed on the T2D effect (LD-aware GLS for the cis classes, IVW with multiplicative random effects
genome-wide), and the AD effect per mmol/L of 2 h glucose is their ratio:
$\hat\theta_{\text{mmol}} = \hat\theta_{AD}/\hat\theta_{2h}$, with
$\text{SE} \approx |\hat\theta_{\text{mmol}}|\sqrt{(\text{SE}_{AD}/\hat\theta_{AD})^2 + (\text{SE}_{2h}/\hat\theta_{2h})^2}$.
This treats MAGIC and the AD GWAS as independent samples. KATP minus comparator differences are
tested with $z = \Delta/\sqrt{\text{SE}_1^2 + \text{SE}_2^2}$, since the groups share no variants.
Two KATP sensitivity rows: without rs113264182 (the variant that flips sign in Kunkle), and rs5215
alone (Wald ratios).

```{r katp-specificity-data}
# Sections 8-9 add the Uffelmann 2026 replication outcomes (post-freeze, raw; SlopeHunter not identified)
datasets_all <- c(datasets, uff_newc = "gwas_ad_uffelmann_newc", uff_cc = "gwas_ad_uffelmann_cc")
labels_all   <- c(labels, uff_newc = "AD, Uffelmann new cohorts (independent)",
                  uff_cc = "AD, Uffelmann clinical only")
katp_reg  <-\(d) filter(d, !(chr == 11 & between(pos, 16.9e6, 17.9e6)), !(chr == 7 & between(pos, 43.7e6, 44.7e6)))
ivw_mre   <- function(bx, by, se) { f <- wls_mre(by, cbind(bx), se); c(b = unname(f$b[[1]]), se = sqrt(f$V[1, 1])) }
cis_gls   <- function(x) {
  Rk <- ld_matrix(x$SNP, bim, bfile, plink2); x <- x[match(rownames(Rk), x$SNP), ]
  s <- if_else(x$ea == bim$a1[match(x$SNP, bim$SNP)], 1, -1); Rk <- Rk * outer(s, s)
  if (nrow(x) == 1) Rk <- matrix(1)
  a <- gls_ratio(x$beta_t2d, x$beta_y, x$se_y, Rk); g <- gls_ratio(x$beta_t2d, x$beta_2h, x$se_2h, Rk)
  tibble(n = nrow(x), b_ad = a[["b"]], se_ad = a[["se"]], b_2h = g[["b"]], se_2h = g[["se"]])
}
dt_all <- read_csv("results/pipeline/contrast/drug_target_snps.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(set == "primary", drug_class %in% c("katp_secretagogue", "glucokinase"))
cis_groups <- bind_rows(
  dt_all |> filter(drug_class == "katp_secretagogue") |> mutate(group = "KATP (KCNJ11/ABCC8), all variants"),
  dt_all |> filter(drug_class == "katp_secretagogue", SNP != "rs113264182") |> mutate(group = "KATP without rs113264182"),
  dt_all |> filter(SNP == "rs5215") |> mutate(group = "KATP, rs5215 (E23K proxy) alone"),
  dt_all |> filter(drug_class == "glucokinase") |> mutate(group = "Glucokinase (GCK)")) |>
  group_by(outcome, arm, group) |> group_modify(\(x, ...) cis_gls(x)) |> ungroup()

iod <- read_csv("results/pipeline/contrast/instrument_outcome_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(set == "primary") |> katp_reg()
gw_groups <- bind_rows(
  iod |> filter(grepl("^Beta cell", cluster)) |> mutate(group = "Beta cell, genome-wide"),
  iod |> filter(cluster == "Beta cell -PI") |> mutate(group = "Beta cell -PI"),
  iod |> filter(cluster == "Beta cell +PI") |> mutate(group = "Beta cell +PI"),
  iod |> mutate(group = "All primary T2D instruments")) |>
  group_by(outcome, arm, group) |>
  group_modify(\(x, ...) { a <- ivw_mre(x$beta_t2d, x$beta_y, x$se_y); g <- ivw_mre(x$beta_t2d, x$beta_2h, x$se_2h)
    tibble(n = nrow(x), b_ad = a[["b"]], se_ad = a[["se"]], b_2h = g[["b"]], se_2h = g[["se"]]) }) |> ungroup()

spec <- bind_rows(cis_groups, gw_groups) |>
  mutate(b_mmol = b_ad / b_2h, se_mmol = abs(b_mmol) * sqrt((se_ad / b_ad)^2 + (se_2h / b_2h)^2),
         outcome_lab = factor(labels_all[c(ad_bellenguez.slopehunter = "ad_sh", ad_bellenguez.raw = "ad_raw",
                                           ad_kunkle.raw = "ad_kun", ad_uffelmann_newc.raw = "uff_newc",
                                           ad_uffelmann_cc.raw = "uff_cc")[paste(outcome, arm, sep = ".")]],
                              levels = labels_all),
         group = factor(group, levels = c("KATP (KCNJ11/ABCC8), all variants", "KATP without rs113264182",
                                          "KATP, rs5215 (E23K proxy) alone", "Glucokinase (GCK)",
                                          "Beta cell, genome-wide", "Beta cell -PI", "Beta cell +PI",
                                          "All primary T2D instruments")))
```

## 9. The vascular KATP channel: ABCC9/KCNJ8 (SUR2/Kir6.1)

If channel-family biology matters, the other KATP channel, made of Kir6.1 and SUR2 (*KCNJ8* and
*ABCC9*, chr12p12.1) and mainly found in vascular smooth muscle and pericytes, is worth a look. *ABCC9*
variants, notably rs704180, have been linked to hippocampal sclerosis of aging. These subunits are
not targets of the T2D drugs in the frozen drug-target map (sulfonylureas bind SUR1), so this is a
regional lookup, not an MR. A null here would not count against the KCNJ11 result, since the two
channels act in different tissues.

```{r abcc9-data}
region12 <- list(chr = "12", start = 21.6e6, end = 22.4e6)   # LDHB 21.79, KCNJ8 21.92, ABCC9 21.95-22.09 Mb
reg12 <- purrr::map(datasets_all, \(t) { x <- as.data.table(tar_read_raw(t))
  x[as.character(chr) == region12$chr & pos >= region12$start & pos <= region12$end] })
# Effective number of independent tests among common variants (Li & Ji 2005), for a region-wide threshold
snps12 <- reg12$ad_sh[eaf > 0.01 & eaf < 0.99 & SNP %in% bim$SNP, SNP]
ev12   <- abs(eigen(ld_matrix(snps12, bim, bfile, plink2), only.values = TRUE)$values)
meff12 <- sum((ev12 >= 1) + (ev12 - floor(ev12)))
```

```{r abcc9-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=13}

                  end = c(21.811e6, 21.928e6, 22.094e6))
purrr::imap_dfr(reg12, \(x, k) x[, .(SNP, pos, p, dataset = labels_all[[k]])]) |>
  mutate(dataset = factor(dataset, levels = labels_all)) |>
  ggplot(aes(pos / 1e6, -log10(p))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = genes12$start / 1e6, xmax = genes12$end / 1e6, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
           fill = "#FFCB05", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, SNP %in% c("rs704180", "rs2077105")), colour = "#9a3324", size = 2.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05 / meff12), linetype = "dashed", colour = "#2F65A7") +
  facet_wrap(~ dataset, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "chr12 position (Mb, GRCh37); shaded: LDHB, KCNJ8, ABCC9",
       y = expression(-log[10]~p),
       caption = sprintf("Red: rs704180 (ABCC9) and rs2077105 (T2D lead). Dashed: 0.05/%d effective tests.", round(meff12))) +
  theme_fm
```

```{r abcc9-leads}
  top <- x[order(p)][1]
  rbind(x[SNP %in% c("rs704180", "rs2077105")], top)[, .(Dataset = labels_all[[k]], SNP, pos, ea, oa,
                                                       beta = round(beta, 4), se = round(se, 4), p = format(p, digits = 2))] |>
    unique() }) |>
```

From the GTEx v8 portal (single-tissue eQTLs, looked up for this section): rs2077105, the T2D lead,
is an eQTL for *LDHB* (lung, oesophagus muscularis) and shows no *KCNJ8* or *ABCC9* association.
rs704180 is an *ABCC9* eQTL in adrenal gland (p = 4×10⁻¹³) and caudate (p = 2×10⁻⁵).

## Reading the results: KATP specificity and SUR2

Sections 8 and 9 were first run on Bellenguez and Kunkle. The Uffelmann 2026 (PGC-ALZ3) files were
added afterwards as replication outcomes: the **new-cohorts** meta-analysis shares no cohorts with
Bellenguez, so it is the independent test, while the **clinical-only** analysis is larger but overlaps
Bellenguez's cohorts. SlopeHunter could not be estimated for either Uffelmann file (raw lifespan–AD
correlation 0.03–0.05, as for Kunkle), so both are uncorrected. Neither file contains rs113264182 or
rs1557763, so the KATP class has five variants there.

**In Bellenguez, KATP looked special.** Per mmol/L of genetically raised 2 h glucose, the KATP class
gave an AD odds ratio of about 1.5 (SlopeHunter-corrected), against 1.08 for GCK and 1.12 for the
genome-wide beta-cell variants (KATP vs GCK p ≈ 0.03). Part of the gap is on the glucose side: per
unit of T2D liability, KATP variants raise 2 h glucose less than half as much as GCK variants (0.57 vs
1.40 mmol/L).

**In the independent cohorts, KATP replicates but does not stand out.** The KATP class gives OR 1.29
per log-odds of T2D (p = 0.007), close to Bellenguez's 1.27, and 1.58 per mmol/L of 2 h glucose. But
GCK (1.25 per mmol/L) and the genome-wide beta-cell variants (1.22) now also raise AD, and the KATP
excess is no longer significant (vs GCK p = 0.23; vs beta-cell p = 0.19). In the clinical-only file
nothing differs (all p > 0.25), with beta-cell variants at 1.14 and all T2D instruments at 1.14 per
mmol/L (both nominally significant).

**The E23K proxy is not what replicates.** rs5215 gives a Wald ratio of 0.11 per log-odds of T2D in
both Uffelmann files, less than half its Bellenguez value (0.27). The new-cohorts KATP estimate comes
mainly from two other KCNJ11-region variants (rs1800467, rs16933952).

**Overall.** T2D liability acting through insulin secretion raises AD risk, and that now holds in an
independent sample, KATP variants included. The suggestion that the KATP channel adds something
beyond the glucose it causes rested on Bellenguez alone and did not replicate.

**Caveats.** All comparisons are nominal. The ratio-of-ratios standard error assumes MAGIC and the AD
GWAS are independent. The new-cohorts file includes the Million Veteran Program, which is also in
Suzuki T2D; that overlap biases every group slightly towards the observational T2D–AD association.

**No AD signal at ABCC9/KCNJ8 in any dataset.** No variant in the 800 kb window passes the region-wide
threshold (p < 2.1×10⁻⁴) in Bellenguez, Kunkle or either Uffelmann file; the closest is rs10161132
(p = 4×10⁻⁴, Uffelmann clinical-only), about 300 kb from KCNJ8. rs704180, the ABCC9 variant
linked to hippocampal sclerosis of aging, is null everywhere (p 0.06–0.42). The Bellenguez top hit
(rs117295320) does not replicate. The region's genome-wide T2D signal (rs2077105) is an *LDHB* eQTL with
no KCNJ8/ABCC9 effect and no AD association. There is no support for the vascular SUR2/Kir6.1 channel.
